title: cornfield in another app: the interface as web components
summary: The explorer becomes an engine a page can make more than one of, in pieces that each own their markup. cornfield's own page mounts the pieces in the document; a new components package wraps the same pieces as web components, built with StencilRS, for another app to put on its own page. The server learns to answer a listed sibling origin: reads, and the review decision. The host app node stands for any app that embeds cornfield; it is not something to build.

add.label: components
add.desc: The web components: thin StencilRS shells that each mount one piece of the explorer's engine in their own root. Built with Vite; the only part of cornfield with a build step.

add.label: instance.js
add.desc: Makes one running explorer: its state, its root element, a fetch bound to a base address, its strings, and how its pieces tell each other something changed. A page can make more than one.

add.label: page.js
add.desc: cornfield's own page shell: makes the one instance for the document, mounts every piece, and turns the address bar's deep links into the properties a host app would set.

add.label: embed.js
add.desc: What a listed origin may ask: the CORS answer for reads, the check on writes (same origin, or a listed origin on the same site), and where sign-in may return to. With no origin listed, every response is as before.

add.label: A host app
add.desc: Any app on a sibling subdomain that puts cornfield's components on its own page. An archetype for the scenarios, never a named product.

set.desc: The shape of one instance's state. No longer a shared object: each instance has its own.

change.why: 31 modules import one shared state, so two maps on a page would share one selection

set.desc: Starts cornfield's own page through the page shell.

change.why: start-up, deep links and document-level listeners belong to the page, not to the pieces

set.desc: The map's look, read from the tokens on the instance's root element and the theme's images from the instance's base address.

change.why: tokens are read from the html element and images from a fixed path, which a component in another page cannot use

set.desc: The Work panel, split into pieces that each own their markup, with native dialogs.

change.why: 2,649 lines in one module, with document-level focus traps

set.desc: The HTTP server: routes, headers, the sign-in gate, and the answer to a listed sibling origin. Serves the built components.

change.why: another origin's page can read nothing today: there are no CORS headers

set.desc: Proposals, their reviews and the decision. A write is taken from the server's own page, or from a listed origin on the same site.

change.why: the review decision must work from inside a host app

set.desc: Sign-in with GitHub or Forgejo (OAuth), sessions in an HttpOnly cookie, the admins-only guard every route passes through, and a return after sign-in to cornfield itself or to a listed origin.

change.why: a maintainer who signs in from the host app should land back in it

set.desc: Reads and checks cornfield.config.js, with embed.origins: the exact origins that may embed cornfield, empty by default.

change.why: which origins are trusted is the maintainer's decision, written down

scenarios.title: The maintainer reviews and approves a proposal without leaving the host app

steps.text: A task's page holds one tag, the review, with the server's address and the proposal's name.
The tag makes its own instance and mounts the map, the changes and the decision inside it.
The host's origin is listed, so the reads are answered, with the maintainer's session.
The map narrows to the change. Selecting here moves nothing else on the host's page.
Approve is a write from a listed origin on the same site: taken, and posted as the maintainer.
The tag tells the host the decision, and the host moves its task on.

scenarios.title: A page that is not listed gets nothing

steps.text: The list of origins is empty, or does not hold this page's origin.
A read gets no CORS answer, so the browser gives the page nothing.
A write is refused, as it is today.

scenarios.title: A host shows a map from data it fetched itself

steps.text: The host fetches a topology by its own means and sets it on the map tag.
The map draws it. No cornfield server is asked for anything.
A click on a node leaves as an event; the host opens its own panel.
